questions.stem: Rohan walks 5 km towards North, then turns right and walks 5 km. In which direction is he now with respect to his starting point?
questions.explanation: From start O, Rohan goes 5 km North then turns right (East) and walks 5 km. He is now to the North-East of O, equidistant in both directions.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A man walks 8 km South, then turns left and walks 6 km. What is his straight-line distance from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Walking South and turning left means facing East. South 8 km + East 6 km form a right triangle. Distance = √(8² + 6²) = √(64 + 36) = √100 = 10 km. **Short Trick:** 6-8-10 is a standard Pythagorean triple (multiple of 3-4-5).
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A person is facing North. He turns 90° clockwise. Which direction is he now facing?
questions.explanation: Clockwise sequence: North → East → South → West → North. A 90° clockwise turn from North = East.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A person is facing South and turns 180°. Which direction is he now facing?
questions.explanation: A 180° turn always reverses direction. South → North.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Priya walks 4 km North, then 3 km East, then 4 km South, then 3 km West. Where is she relative to the starting point?
questions.explanation: North 4 km and South 4 km cancel out; East 3 km and West 3 km cancel out. Net displacement = 0. She returns to the starting point.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A man is facing East (direction of sunrise). He takes two consecutive left turns of 90° each. Which direction is he now facing?
questions.explanation: Facing East: 1st left turn (90° anticlockwise) → North. 2nd left turn → West.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Starting from a point, Amit walks 7 km East, then 4 km North, then 7 km West. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: East 7 km and West 7 km cancel each other. Net movement = 4 km North. He is 4 km North of the starting point.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Priti walks 15 km West, then 10 km North, then 15 km East. How far and in which direction is she from the starting point?
questions.explanation: West 15 km and East 15 km cancel. Net movement = 10 km North. She is 10 km North of start.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: In the morning, a man's shadow falls exactly behind him. Which direction is he facing?
questions.explanation: In the morning, the Sun rises in the East, so shadows fall towards the West. If the shadow is behind him, he is facing East (Sun is in front).
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A car travels 12 km North, then turns right and travels 16 km East. What is the straight-line distance from the starting point?
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A person is facing West and turns 90° anticlockwise. Which direction is he now facing?
questions.explanation: Anticlockwise sequence: North → West → South → East → North. A 90° anticlockwise turn from West = South.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Initially facing North, a person first turns 45° clockwise, then turns 180° clockwise. Which direction is he finally facing?
questions.explanation: North + 45° clockwise = North-East. North-East + 180° = opposite direction = South-West.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A man walks 6 km East and then 8 km North. What is his straight-line distance from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Distance = √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 km. **Short Trick:** 6-8-10 is a standard Pythagorean triple.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A person is walking towards the South-West. What direction is directly behind him?
questions.explanation: The direction opposite to South-West is North-East. If you walk SW, behind you is NE.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A person faces North, then turns 90° clockwise, then turns 45° anticlockwise, then turns 45° clockwise. Which direction is he finally facing?
questions.explanation: North + 90° CW = East. East + 45° ACW = North-East. NE + 45° CW = East (NE is 45° ACW of E, so +45° CW returns to E). Final direction: East.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: From her house, Riya walks 3 km North, then 4 km West, then 3 km South. How far and in which direction is she from her house?
questions.explanation: North 3 km and South 3 km cancel. Net displacement = 4 km West. She is 4 km West of her house.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A is to the South of B, and C is to the East of B. In which direction is A with respect to C?
questions.explanation: Place B at origin. A is South of B → A is at (0, −k). C is East of B → C is at (+m, 0). A relative to C: A is to the South and West of C, i.e., South-West.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A person walks 4 km East, 3 km South, 4 km West, and then 2 km North. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: East 4 and West 4 cancel. South 3 − North 2 = 1 km South. Net position: 1 km South of start.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Starting from point P, a person walks 5 km East, 3 km North, 8 km West, and 4 km South. What is his distance from P?
questions.explanation: Net East-West: 5E − 8W = 3W. Net North-South: 3N − 4S = 1S. Final position: 3 km West, 1 km South of P. Distance = √(3² + 1²) = √10 km.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A man starts from home and walks 5 km North, 4 km East, 3 km South, and 2 km West. What is his distance and direction from home?
questions.explanation: Net East-West: 4E − 2W = 2E. Net North-South: 5N − 3S = 2N. Position: 2 km East, 2 km North. Distance = √(2² + 2²) = √8 = 2√2 km, direction North-East.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Suresh walks 6 km East, then 8 km North, then 6 km West. How far is he from the starting point and in which direction?
questions.explanation: East 6 km and West 6 km cancel. Net displacement = 8 km North. He is 8 km North of start.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A person walks 10 km in the North-East direction, then 10 km in the South-East direction. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: NE 10 km gives (10/√2) East + (10/√2) North. SE 10 km gives (10/√2) East + (10/√2) South. N and S components cancel. Total East = 20/√2 = 10√2 km.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A person is facing the direction exactly opposite to where the Sun sets. Which direction is he facing?
questions.explanation: The Sun sets in the West. The direction exactly opposite to West is East.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A man walks 6 km East, then 3 km North, then 6 km West. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: East 6 km and West 6 km cancel. Net displacement = 3 km North. He is 3 km North of start.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A man walks 3 km in the North-East direction, then 3 km in the South-East direction. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: NE 3 km: (3/√2) East + (3/√2) North. SE 3 km: (3/√2) East + (3/√2) South. N and S cancel. Total East = 6/√2 = 3√2 km East.
questions.subject: Reasoning
